title: October 2026: the stories of the month
description: The SGit Newsroom's October 2026: the stories big enough to get a site of their own, led by the two PHP flaws disclosed on 21 October, with links up to the year and the newsroom and down to each story.
lead_html: One site per story, built from captured evidence. This month has one so far, and it is the one that took government websites offline across Europe: two critical flaws in the PHP engine, found with AI help, leaked two days early, patched on 21 October. The newsroom's own daily coverage is on newsroom.sgit.ai; this page is the index of what became a story.

items.title: php2shell: the two PHP flaws of October 2026, tracked as evidence
items.blurb_html: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619: what is established, who said what and when, the code of the fix read from php-src, the numbers that do not add up, sixteen agencies compared, what was taken offline and what was compromised, detection and defence, and a briefing for every role from the board to the developer. Every claim carries a status and its sources; every source is captured and hashed.
